texts: mixed: the visibility, the vantage from Aelmere, the morning and the date are all covered and both per-spire rules fire, but "clearly" is recorded as a degree of the visibility state rather than of the spires, so "how visible were the spires?" finds nothing. That is a slot slip inside the translator, not a trap in your wording — dropping "clearly" would lose content and no other phrasing moves the atom, so keep the sentence as written. Separate note for your whole calendar: "day 575 of Year 2" lands in the day-of-month slot, which has no room for a day-of-year count, and there is no other term for it yet.
good. the keepers' group, the walking, its goal and the base-as-part-of-the-cliff link are all covered as a plain past event.

good. "each cliff-spire" becomes a fireable per-spire rule ranging over the spire group introduced in the first sentence, with each spire's own sky-cats and the on-that-spire link kept, plus the "each" quantifier word recorded.
good. the fourteen-member sky-cat group with its count, the keepers as the counters, and past tense are all there.

bad: the twelve is asserted as a real group of twelve sky-cats, so the Year-1 figure enters the knowledge base as fact and the whole fourteen-versus-twelve point is lost; the past perfect also leaves no ordering atom against the keepers' count, so the "had" anteriority drops. Put the figure inside a reported clause and name the anchor: "Before that count, the census of Year 1 had estimated that there were twelve sky-cats."

bad: "logged X as an estimate" has no licensed form, so the classification is flattened into a bare world fact — the census simply IS an estimate in the knowledge base, with nothing tying that classification to the Council's log. Split the recording from the classification and put the classification in a finite reported clause: "The Council logged the census and said that the census was an estimate."
